21: /// A matcher for implementing "word match" semantics.
22: #[derive(Debug)]
23: pub(crate) struct WordMatcher {
24:     /// The regex which is roughly `(?:^|\W)(<original pattern>)(?:$|\W)`.
25:     regex: Regex,
26:     /// The HIR that produced the regex above. We don't keep the HIR for the
27:     /// `original` regex.
28:     ///
29:     /// We put this in an `Arc` because by the time it gets here, it won't
30:     /// change. And because cloning and dropping an `Hir` is somewhat expensive
31:     /// due to its deep recursive representation.
32:     chir: Arc<ConfiguredHIR>,
33:     /// The original regex supplied by the user, which we use in a fast path
34:     /// to try and detect matches before deferring to slower engines.
35:     original: Regex,
36:     /// A map from capture group name to capture group index.
37:     names: HashMap<String, usize>,
38:     /// A thread-safe pool of reusable buffers for finding the match offset of
39:     /// the inner group.
40:     caps: Arc<Pool<Captures, PoolFn>>,
41: }
42: 
43: impl Clone for WordMatcher {
44:     fn clone(&self) -> WordMatcher {
45:         // We implement Clone manually so that we get a fresh Pool such that it
46:         // can set its own thread owner. This permits each thread usings `caps`
47:         // to hit the fast path.
48:         //
49:         // Note that cloning a regex is "cheap" since it uses reference
50:         // counting internally.
51:         let re = self.regex.clone();
52:         WordMatcher {
53:             regex: self.regex.clone(),
54:             chir: Arc::clone(&self.chir),
55:             original: self.original.clone(),
56:             names: self.names.clone(),
57:             caps: Arc::new(Pool::new(Box::new(move || re.create_captures()))),
58:         }
59:     }
60: }
61: 
62: impl WordMatcher {
63:     /// Create a new matcher from the given pattern that only produces matches
64:     /// that are considered "words."
65:     ///
66:     /// The given options are used to construct the regular expression
67:     /// internally.
68:     pub(crate) fn new(chir: ConfiguredHIR) -> Result<WordMatcher, Error> {
69:         let original = chir.clone().into_anchored().to_regex()?;
70:         let chir = Arc::new(chir.into_word()?);
71:         let regex = chir.to_regex()?;
72:         let caps = Arc::new(Pool::new({
73:             let regex = regex.clone();
74:             Box::new(move || regex.create_captures()) as PoolFn
75:         }));
76: 
77:         let mut names = HashMap::new();
78:         let it = regex.group_info().pattern_names(PatternID::ZERO);
79:         for (i, optional_name) in it.enumerate() {
80:             if let Some(name) = optional_name {
81:                 names.insert(name.to_string(), i.checked_sub(1).unwrap());
82:             }
83:         }
84:         Ok(WordMatcher { regex, chir, original, names, caps })
85:     }
86: 
87:     /// Return the underlying regex used to match at word boundaries.
88:     ///
89:     /// The original regex is in the capture group at index 1.
90:     pub(crate) fn regex(&self) -> &Regex {
91:         &self.regex
92:     }
93: 
94:     /// Return the underlying HIR for the regex used to match at word
95:     /// boundaries.
96:     pub(crate) fn chir(&self) -> &ConfiguredHIR {
97:         &self.chir
98:     }
99: }
100: 
101: impl ConfiguredHIR {
102:     /// Attempt to do a fast confirmation of a word match that covers a subset
103:     /// (but hopefully a big subset) of most cases. Ok(Some(..)) is returned
104:     /// when a match is found. Ok(None) is returned when there is definitively
105:     /// no match. Err(()) is returned when this routine could not detect
106:     /// whether there was a match or not.
107:     fn fast_find(
108:         &self,
109:         matcher: &WordMatcher,
110:         haystack: &[u8],
111:         at: usize,
112:     ) -> Result<Option<Match>, ()> {
113:         // This is a bit hairy. The whole point here is to avoid running a
114:         // slower regex engine to extract capture groups. Remember, our word
115:         // regex looks like this:
116:         //
117:         //     (^|\W)(<original regex>)(\W|$)
118:         //
119:         // What we want are the match offsets of <original regex>. So in the
120:         // easy/common case, the original regex will be sandwiched between
121:         // two codepoints that are in the \W class. So our approach here is to
122:         // look for a match of the overall word regexp, strip the \W ends and
123:         // then check whether the original regex matches what's left. If so,
124:         // then we are guaranteed a correct match.
125:         //
126:         // This only works though if we know that the match is sandwiched
127:         // between two \W codepoints. This only occurs when neither ^ nor $
128:         // match. This in turn only occurs when the match is at either the
129:         // beginning or end of the haystack. In either of those cases, we
130:         // declare defeat and defer to the slower implementation.
131:         //
132:         // The reason why we cannot handle the ^/$ cases here is because we
133:         // can't assume anything about the original pattern. (Try commenting
134:         // out the checks for ^/$ below and run the tests to see examples.)
135:         if !std::ptr::eq(self, matcher.chir.as_ref()) {
136:             return Err(());
137:         }
138:         if !matcher.names.is_empty() {
139:             return Err(());
140:         }
141:         {
142:             let caps = matcher.caps.get();
143:             if caps.group_info().all_group_len() < 2 {
144:                 return Err(());
145:             }
146:         }
147:         let start_look = if self.config().crlf {
148:             Look::StartCRLF
149:         } else {
150:             Look::StartLF
151:         };
152:         let end_look = if self.config().crlf {
153:             Look::EndCRLF
154:         } else {
155:             Look::EndLF
156:         };
157:         let wrapped = match self.hir().kind() {
158:             HirKind::Concat(parts) if parts.len() == 3 => {
159:                 let start_ok = match parts[0].kind() {
160:                     HirKind::Alternation(alts) => alts.iter().any(|hir| {
161:                         matches!(
162:                             hir.kind(),
163:                             HirKind::Look(look) if *look == start_look
164:                         )
165:                     }),
166:                     _ => false,
167:                 };
168:                 let end_ok = match parts[2].kind() {
169:                     HirKind::Alternation(alts) => alts.iter().any(|hir| {
170:                         matches!(
171:                             hir.kind(),
172:                             HirKind::Look(look) if *look == end_look
173:                         )
174:                     }),
175:                     _ => false,
176:                 };
177:                 start_ok && end_ok
178:             }
179:             _ => false,
180:         };
181:         if !wrapped {
182:             return Err(());
183:         }
184:         let input = Input::new(haystack).span(at..haystack.len());
185:         let mut cand = match matcher.regex.find(input) {
186:             None => return Ok(None),
187:             Some(m) => Match::new(m.start(), m.end()),
188:         };
189:         if cand.start() == 0 || cand.end() == haystack.len() {
190:             return Err(());
191:         }
192:         let (_, slen) = bstr::decode_utf8(&haystack[cand]);
193:         let (_, elen) = bstr::decode_last_utf8(&haystack[cand]);
194:         let new_start = cand.start() + slen;
195:         let new_end = cand.end() - elen;
196:         // This occurs the original regex can match the empty string. In this
197:         // case, just bail instead of trying to get it right here since it's
198:         // likely a pathological case.
199:         if new_start > new_end {
200:             return Err(());
201:         }
202:         cand = cand.with_start(new_start).with_end(new_end);
203:         if matcher.original.is_match(&haystack[cand]) {
204:             Ok(Some(cand))
205:         } else {
206:             Err(())
207:         }
208:     }
209: }
